briefing.opening: Good day, everyone. We will now commence the climate change expert spokesperson briefing for September 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis and Carbon Budget Warning
sections.content: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) has warned that the carbon budget to limit global temperature rise to within 1.5℃ is only enough for three more years, emphasizing the need to maintain this goal despite potential failure to achieve it [11]. Amidst this urgent situation, climate change threatens human rights issues [86], increases the risk of mycotoxins [88], and even impacts our preferred tastes [93]. Localized signs of climate change, such as the appearance of sharks in Busan's North Port, have also been observed [12]. Notably, Morocco is among the African countries most exposed to climate change risks [95], and Scotland's infrastructure is struggling with 'storms' caused by climate change [100], indicating direct impacts globally. Despite the critical need for international solidarity [97], movements hindering climate action, such as the Trump administration's easing of clean car regulations [105] and the influence of the fossil fuel industry extending to university research [106], have also been detected, adding to concerns.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Strengthening Domestic Carbon Neutrality Policies and Institutional Reforms
sections.content: Domestically, the institutional foundation for responding to the climate crisis is being strengthened. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries is pushing for reforms to the aquaculture disaster insurance in preparation for accelerating climate change [1, 6], and the Greenhouse Gas Inventory & Research Center discussed its role as a dedicated research institution for climate crisis response [3, 16]. Notably, the National Institute of Climate Science, which will serve as a 'think tank' for greenhouse gas reduction, is set to launch within the year to strengthen its function of monitoring greenhouse gas reduction implementation [4, 15, 17]. At the local government level, Gyeongsangbuk-do is accelerating direct emission reductions by elevating its Administrative Vice Governor to a responsible official and reorganizing its task force to achieve the 2050 carbon neutrality goal [18, 27, 29, 37, 56]. Furthermore, the Chungnam Provincial Council launched a research group to realize 'Carbon Neutrality 2045' and has begun actively establishing a policy framework by exploring the utilization of Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) technologies and promoting related ordinances [20, 21, 24, 33, 36, 39, 44, 50, 59].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Technological Innovation Efforts
sections.content: In the renewable energy sector, active development and innovation are taking place both domestically and internationally. Korea has completed an international development cooperation project to construct a MW-class solar power plant in the highlands of Tajikistan [8, 70, 82], and the new president of the Korea Institute of Energy Research expressed aspirations to lead a 'vertical leap' in carbon neutrality [30]. Furthermore, High-Temperature Gas-cooled Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) have been proposed as a carbon-neutral solution for key industries such as steel and petrochemicals [22], and Envision Energy has suggested green ammonia as a means for renewable energy storage and transportation [65]. However, challenges have also emerged in the process of expanding renewable energy, including concerns about landslides due to solar and wind facilities built on slopes [62] and regional regulatory differences, such as Jangseong County still completely prohibiting the installation of floating solar power [76]. Additionally, international project implementation faces difficulties, with 46 renewable energy projects in Vietnam failing to finalize price contracts [80], and some investment-related challenges have been reported, such as Gresham House Renewable Energy VCT 1 entering liquidation [68, 73].

sections.title: 📰 Climate Change Adaptation and Expanding Citizen Participation
sections.content: Efforts to adapt to climate change and expand citizen participation are also being pursued in various ways. Domestically, a special exhibition on climate change is being held at the Baekdudaegan National Arboretum [2], and discussions are taking place on the role and value of trees in the era of climate change [5], indicating active efforts to adapt to climate change and raise public awareness. The Jeonnam Gwangju Agricultural Technology Center explored adaptation in the agricultural sector through a special lecture on future agricultural response strategies to abnormal climate conditions [9, 14]. Furthermore, eco-friendly functional materials for urban climate change adaptation are gaining attention [7], and Central Park is also addressing climate change [96], demonstrating that practical adaptation measures are being sought. Meanwhile, Gwangju City is operating a new sign-up event for the Carbon Neutrality Point System throughout October, encouraging citizens' participation in energy saving [19, 40, 49]. Cheongju City and Janghang Elementary School Social Cooperative are also spreading a culture of everyday carbon neutrality through carbon neutrality practice campaigns and pickle donations [25, 54]. Internationally, a new poll shows climate change re-emerging as a top priority for people [91], and Chicago museums are encouraging people to talk about climate change [85], thereby raising public awareness.

briefing.closing: Today's climate news demonstrates that despite global crisis warnings, diverse policy efforts, technological innovations, and active citizen participation are taking place both domestically and internationally. We hope these endeavors will bear fruit and accelerate the realization of a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
